chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
If matters get mixed up then the last ones should be appreciated according to the previous one.
ai.seo_question: How to evaluate ambiguous matters based on their initial state?
ai.summary: This maxim, central to Shia jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh), establishes the principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity), where the initial state of certainty prevails until proven otherwise by subsequent evidence. It provides a critical methodological tool for scholars to resolve ambiguity in legal rulings and personal status by anchoring judgment in the established origin. This reflects the broader epistemological reliance on stable foundations amidst changing circumstances.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 76. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
If matters get mixed up then the last ones should be appreciated according to the previous one. [1]
